mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.2 percentage points, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the trigger period, or FEDFUNDS increase is ≤ 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) above the prior month's level is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) over the 60-day horizon following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (residential construction) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 5%, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting optimism about future economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA of HOUST by at least 5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the signal period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of over 2% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary pressures.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment rate) by at least 0.5 percentage points over a month increases the probability of a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return by reducing policy uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month AND UNRATE < previous month by ≥ 0.5%
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day return (p > 0.05) when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS (retail sales) of 10% or more for two consecutive months is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to strong consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month by ≥ 10% AND RSAFS next month > previous month by ≥ 10%
failure_condition: No significant positive return (p > 0.05) when trigger is satisfied.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL (CPI) inflation above 3%, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market expectations of rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the inflation condition.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) above 2% followed by a subsequent month's rise of at least 1% predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as near-term demand momentum is detected.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month by ≥ 2% AND GDPC1 next month > previous month by ≥ 1%
failure_condition: No significant positive return (p > 0.05) within the 5-day horizon after trigger.
